x: Ron paired with "Pub" Childs, got well ahead during the first four laps of the 1415 yards circuit, but the pace then told and Len Bishop, paired with Eric Gebbett, who had been running a fast but steady race closed up gradually taking the lead on the 5th lap, a lead which they never lost again during the race.
The "B" Team slowly progressed after their bad start and thanks to good runs by Collis, Len Bishop and Hitchcock, pulled up to 14th position. 30 teams finished.
Len Bishop ran last and seemed determined that those behind him should remain so and he put up the fastest time of the day with a time only Brown has beaten for us.

Len Bishop agreed to run in the 440 and did a time which satisfied everyone. In the 880 we were represented by George Davidson who just failed to catch Ken Norris in the straight and Dave Hooper who managed a personal best over the distance.

Knight of Essex Beagles was the individual winner completing the course in record time and finishing in front of Sando. Pete Bagnall was our first man home in 11th position and supported by Masters, Short and L. Bishop, we gained 3rd place in the team event.

The end of the first lap saw George Stace and Len Bishop were leading with several other teams within striking distance. This pair however, could not maintain their position and soon a terrific battle was taking place with Eric Gebbet paired that Alan Black and Bill Bird paired with Jim Edgar.

Len Bishop also coming into the team as a reserve, had the unenviable task of coping with Douglas of the Beagles and Ralph Dunkley of the Poly and although he drove himself to the last ounce, he was forced to give ground to this pair and to Porter of Finchley and we were once more back to fourth.

Len Bishop showed a welcome return to form in taking 4th place and George Flanagan who should have a promising future occupied 5th place. Tooby was running far ahead of his Ilford showing but Short showed little or no enthusiasm for his running.
Len Bishop was on the 6th leg and although he has been a steady performer for some years, he rose above himself and took us up to 6th place, but we still made no impression on the leaders.

Martin and a very close team event over 2 miles gave Herne Hill a one point win over us, Len Bishop being 2nd to Towl. Our field events men, as usual were a tower of strength contributing 31 points in five events.

Pete Bagnall and Len Bishop were 1st and 2nd in the three miles and it was good to see Len out again after an injury. The senior 4 x 440 yards relay of Sexton, Glen, Boreham and Heathfield, won despite good opposition and having already competed during the afternoon in other races.

Len Bishop,in place of our regular first runner,P.Bagnall, who was injured,rose well above the form he had shown of late, giving us a reasonably good start finishing 6th behind Poly,H.H.H Aylesford, Hampstead,and St.Albans in that order.
Road Race, appropriate acknowledgment we feel, of the work put in by Arthur Whitehead. Len Bishop is now a married man, and will of course be doing even more training.

Although still very husky from a heavy cold, Shippen was about the 100 mark with Len Bishop, Eddie Short and Jim Heathfield further back. And so it was, our lads hung on grimly to their early gains and ran out a good third with Jack Brown, a little disappointed perhaps, our first man home.

There our men showed that at least they could hold on to their positions, and after 3 miles Jack had moved up to the twenties, Eric was running extremely well, just outside the hundred; Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Chas Walker and Len Bishop were our scoring team in that order.

Dave Baulch ran well to hold our lead but on the next stage, Len Bishop had to give best to Ellis of T.V.H., and we were now second. A rather unhappy looking 'Jumbo' Masters, whom we welcomed back after a long absence, hung on to our position but we had slipped back on times.

We fielded two teams, and our first stage runners were Len Bishop 'A' team, and G. Stevens 'B' Team, who both ran well, on a stage when positions are rather close, finishing 6th and 18th respectively.
3rd Len Bishop With all due respects to Len this was not his sort of stage, but it is easy to be wise after the event.

A new Club record was put up for this distance by Len Bishop when he finished 11th in 2hrs.30 m.47s. Other Club members taking part were, Eric Gebbett 23rd in 2H.42m.56s., Alan Bishop 29th in 2h.51m.7s. and Eric Bishop 36th in 3h.1m.57s.
We did, However, manage to secure third place behind the very powerful Hull and Thames Valley teams, our scoring team consisting of the three Bishop brothers.

Len Bishop, on the tenth stage, thought we still had a chance, and with a run which gave him the fastest time of the day, picked up one place which brought us up to fifth, only 12 seconds behind the third and fourth teams.
Chas. ran well to finish fifth with Len Bishop pipping his brother Eric for third scoring place. Teams:- 1, Belgrave H. 17 pts. 2, Lincoln Wellington A.C. 30 pts 3, Thames Valley Harriers 33 pts.
Our up and coming member Weate, ran extremely well to gain his first place in a Club championship, filling second place, 20 sec. in front of Len Bishop.

The fact that we could only scrape third place in the team race was mainly due to A.Bishop running some fourteen minutes slower than he did last year. Result:- 5th, L.C.Bishop 1.55.47; 7th, E.Gebbett 1.58.02;

In spite of being fairly new to marathon running both Leonard and Eric Bishop ran very confidently to finish 5th and 8th respectively. Bob Plummer,by gaining 11th place,completed our scoring team which was beaten by T.V.H. by the narrow margin of two points.

Len Bishop, who had been content to hang back in the early stages, now began to move up and at sixteen miles passed Eric at great speed. Maintaining his speed to the end of the race he finished a very good third in the Open Race and was a comfortable winner of the Club Championship.
Len Bishop kept us in third position with 19.02 but could not close the gap on Poly and Malcolm Robinson went off, 1.26 behind, on the seventh stage.

Walker was 12th with 24.24, Len Bishop 17th in 24.57 and Eric Bishop 26.02. Jim Heathfield took over from Collis on the second stage for the 'D' team with Bhatia running for the 'A', Shippen for the 'C' and Conway for the 'E'.

Then came Len Bishop in 3rd. place Eric 9th, Bob Glover (coerced into running by Ken Stimpson) 10th!, with Alan Bishop, Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer running well together in 14th position - 1 min.49 secs. down on the leaders.
Len Bishop, with a season of distance running behind him, was given first leg to sharpen up his speed - as were Dennis Jones and Ken Stimpson, for the 'B' and 'C' teams.

Don Maclean soon went to the front and looked set for a record breaking run with Charlie Walker, Clive Shippen, Eric Gebbett, John Moore and Jumbo Masters forming one group, twenty yards up on Ranjit Bhatia, Len Bishop and Mike Stearman.
10 Stage.Len Bishop(21.16) If Len could have kept up the pace he showed over the first mile we would have wiped out Jim Peters' name from the book, and Belgrave would have moved out of sixth place.

No doubt Alan's physique, which five year's later made him an obvious choice for the honour of helping the Olympic torch on its way to Wembley, recommended him to Syd, though I doubt if the latter realised he was signing on a potential 50-miler and, indirectly, a trio who would be a team in themselves.

When Len Bishop our next scorer arrived we were last of the four, but the very next man to arrive in was find-of-the-season N. Stairs whose effort took us to a narrow team win—four points covering the first four teams.
Bruce and Shippen were lethargic and Lennie Bishop faded after a promising start; but young Alan Morrison should feel encouraged, performing as he did in this his first race over the distance.

We also extend congratulation to Jill and Len Bishop on the birth of their daughter Angela. Eric Bishop won this particular race several years ago with his son Clive and it now only remains for brother Alan to close in for Bishop Harriers!

With three to score for the Jim Peters Trophy our boys beat the Bristol leading trio by 16 points, and in the Fry Trophy competition for six runners our first three boys together with D.W.Jones (55) Len (64) and Alan Bishop (67) beat Epsom & Ewell Harriers by one point after a recount.
